newsitem.title: UK: Better demand boosts NWE heating oil spreads.
newsitem.headline: Better demand boosts NWE heating oil spreads.

text.p: North-west European heating oil differentials firmed on Friday in response to better demand and supply worries, traders said.
"There are some buyers struggling to get covered," one said.
A cargo for first decade August delivery changed hands around $1 firmer at a $2 premium to the front month August IPE futures contract. August IPE closed $2.25 up at $167.50 a tonne.
Heating oil was later assessed firmer at premiums to August IPE of $2 bid and $3 offered.
Traders said the market rose on a perceived scarcity of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil cargoes in the ARA.
That was due to occasional refinery problems in the Netherlands and fears of lower-than-expected output from Ventspils following its August pipeline maintenance.
An August 1-5 cargo of low sulphur diesel changed hands at a firm August IPE +$3.50 cif Hamburg, translating to around August IPE +$5 cif Le Havre.
A prompt low sulphur diesel barge moved unchanged at August IPE +$3.55. Heating oil barges were quiet and talked sporadically at August IPE flat to +50 cents.
